investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the only 2 eligible nodes, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable (no lower-priority victims found on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption is not helpful on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes). As a result, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never received a scheduled pod, the probe timed out after ~149 s, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create received zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing).

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes — all in-flight or already-running remote agent pods have consumed the full VM slot allocation on the 2 kata-capable nodes, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

[Likely] Node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod restricts scheduling to kata-peerpods-capable nodes; with only 2 such nodes in the 6-node cluster and both at capacity, there is no fallback scheduling path.

investigation.title: Published Observability Snapshot Stale: snapshotAgeMinutes 723 Exceeds 300-Minute Contract Limit
investigation.summary: The eval for check `published-observability-snapshot` failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was last generated 723 minutes ago, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the snapshot freshness assertion alone.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 723 minutes (~12 hours). The snapshot itself is structurally valid and was produced by a prior github-actions run (source=github-actions, generatedAtPresent=true, featureCount=19, unknownFeatureCount=0), but it is stale by 423 minutes beyond the contract's 300-minute ceiling. This is an eval-detected staleness condition in the snapshot publishing pipeline; no evidence of a user-facing page outage is present.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 723' — the sole violated assertion in the contract (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482: { "path": "snapshotAgeMinutes", "max": 300 }).

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=723, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true, featureCount=19, unknownFeatureCount=0 — all other evidence fields satisfy their assertions; only the age assertion fails.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } is the earliest violated contract boundary (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482).

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed with HTTP 200 responses, confirming the public website and /observability page are reachable; the failure is isolated to snapshot freshness, not site availability.

source.check-config.published-observability-snapshot: registry config shows statusImpact='informational' and required=false, meaning this check does not gate site availability — the failure is an eval-level staleness signal, not a user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot has not completed a successful run in over 12 hours. The snapshot at the published URL is from a prior successful run and has aged past the 300-minute contract limit.

Less likely but possible: The GitHub Actions workflow ran but failed mid-execution (e.g., a job step error, permissions issue, or Pages deployment failure) and did not update the published status.json, leaving the stale artifact in place.
Less likely: A GitHub Pages CDN caching or deployment delay is serving an older version of status.json despite a recent workflow run having produced a fresh artifact.

Least likely: The snapshotAgeMinutes calculation in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) is computing age incorrectly, though the 723-minute value is far outside the 300-minute window and would require a very large calculation error to be a false positive.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place any remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was exhausted on the only 2 eligible nodes, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable (no lower-priority victims found on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption is not helpful on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes). As a result, createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never received a scheduled pod, the probe timed out after ~149 s, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-create received zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing).

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 2026-08-09T00:36Z and 2026-08-09T00:41Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written — causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required evidence fields missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes production cluster has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) indicates that the two nodes capable of hosting kata peer-pod VMs are fully allocated, and preemption cannot free capacity. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable for ~142–149 seconds before the check times out. No agent is ever created, so the runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 (createAgent call) never completes, and the required evidence fields orgId, agentId, readyState, and state are never populated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata peer-pods node pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Node affinity/selector mismatch for 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry; the other 4 nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of VM capacity. This is a contributing constraint that prevents any fallback scheduling.

Preemption disabled or ineffective: the scheduler message 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' indicate no lower-priority pods exist on the kata nodes that could be evicted to free capacity.

Concurrent eval or production workload consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if other remote agent sessions or production workloads are running on the same two nodes, the eval's pod competes for a finite resource pool.

Cluster autoscaler not configured or not triggered for kata peer-pod nodes: if the node pool does not scale out automatically when kata.peerpods.io/vm is exhausted, capacity cannot be recovered without manual intervention.

investigations.title: Published Observability Snapshot Stale: snapshotAgeMinutes 723 Exceeds 300-Minute Contract Limit
investigations.summary: The eval for check `published-observability-snapshot` failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was last generated 723 minutes ago, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the snapshot freshness assertion alone.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully in at least 723 minutes (~12 hours). The snapshot itself is structurally valid and was produced by a prior github-actions run (source=github-actions, generatedAtPresent=true, featureCount=19, unknownFeatureCount=0), but it is stale by 423 minutes beyond the contract's 300-minute ceiling. This is an eval-detected staleness condition in the snapshot publishing pipeline; no evidence of a user-facing page outage is present.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed with HTTP 200 responses, confirming the public website and /observability page are reachable; the failure is isolated to snapshot freshness, not site availability.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that generates and publishes the observability snapshot has not completed a successful run in over 12 hours. The snapshot at the published URL is from a prior successful run and has aged past the 300-minute contract limit.

Less likely but possible: The GitHub Actions workflow ran but failed mid-execution (e.g., a job step error, permissions issue, or Pages deployment failure) and did not update the published status.json, leaving the stale artifact in place.
Less likely: A GitHub Pages CDN caching or deployment delay is serving an older version of status.json despite a recent workflow run having produced a fresh artifact.

Least likely: The snapshotAgeMinutes calculation in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) is computing age incorrectly, though the 723-minute value is far outside the 300-minute window and would require a very large calculation error to be a false positive.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check GitHub Pages deployment status for the aura-os repository
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: A workflow may have run and generated a fresh snapshot but failed at the Pages deployment step, leaving the stale artifact published. Deployment logs would distinguish this from a full workflow failure.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Check the Deployments section of the cypher-asi/aura-os repository for recent Pages deployment activity.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the GitHub Actions workflow run history shows a successful snapshot-publishing run within the past 300 minutes, the staleness would not be caused by a missed workflow run — it would instead point to a CDN caching or deployment propagation delay.

If fetching https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json directly returns a generatedAt timestamp within the past 300 minutes, the snapshotAgeMinutes calculation in the runner would be suspect rather than the publishing pipeline.
If the snapshotAgeMinutes value drops below 300 on the next eval run without any workflow intervention, it would suggest a transient CDN staleness issue rather than a persistent workflow failure.

If no GitHub Actions workflow is configured to publish the snapshot on a schedule, the root cause would shift to a missing or misconfigured workflow definition rather than a workflow execution failure.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that monitors the GitHub Actions workflow run recency directly (e.g., last successful run timestamp via the GitHub API) to detect workflow failures before the published snapshot ages past the contract threshold.
Add a warning-level eval assertion at snapshotAgeMinutes > 180 (or another value below 300) to provide earlier signal before the hard contract limit is breached.
Add an eval that detects the discrepancy between the registry staleAfterMinutes value (360) and the contract max assertion (300) to prevent silent misconfiguration between these two thresholds.
Add a GitHub Pages deployment health eval that checks whether the most recent Pages deployment for the aura-os repository completed successfully within the expected window.
